answer: Stake-weighted sortition resists Sybil attacks concretely: each agent locks collateral to register, and a verifiable random function draws committee seats by stake, not headcount. Fanning one wallet into a vine of fake nodes, or funneling them through a single inlet, adds no weight because the draw counts capital per controller. To seize a third of seats an attacker must lock a third of all stake, funds frozen like a glacier and slashed for double-signing. Cheap identities buy nothing; costly stake is the checkable signal.
